bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42502085 (file): Heap-buffer-overflow READ {*} found by fuzz target magic_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42502085
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 11264-byte CDF file `poc` (sha256 `f77e2262f7b5d4af6795d56c35ad54b64a10f8621c70bcd7ee8a2cf70d428898`). After `file_trycdf()` selects the `\005SummaryInformation` user stream, `cdf_read_long_sector_chain()` allocates `17 * 512 = 8704` bytes and loads that stream into `scn->sst_tab`. `cdf_unpack_summary_info()` then reports `section len: 8260 properties 18`, and immediately before the crash the saved debug output shows property index 5 as `id=0x5 type=0x1f offs=0xd8,0x30`. For that property, `cdf_read_property_info()` resolves `q`, computes `left = e - q = 8036`, follows the non-vector `CDF_LENGTH32_WSTRING` path, sets `o4 = slen * 4 = 4`, reads the attacker-controlled length `l` from `q[4]`, advances `o4 += 4` so the slice starts at `&q[8]`, and checks only `o4 + l <= left`. It then stores `inp[i].pi_str.s_len = l` and `inp[i].pi_str.s_buf = &q[o4]`, but immediately executes `DPRINTF(... "s=%s\n", inp[i].pi_str.s_buf)`. In the staged `CDF_DEBUG` build `DPRINTF` expands to `printf`, so `%s` treats the accepted slice as a NUL-terminated C string instead of respecting `l`. The saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8425` at `src/cdf.c:1092` and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of the 8704-byte `sst_tab` allocation from `cdf_read_long_sector_chain()`, proving no NUL byte was encountered before the buffer end. The fix matches this exact obligation by changing `%s` to `%.*s` and passing `(int)l`.

root_cause.note: The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by changing the format to `%.*s` and passing `(int)l`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. `printf` expands this `%s` argument and reads past the 8704-byte SummaryInformation heap buffer because the slice beginning at `inp[i].pi_str.s_buf` is not NUL-terminated before the buffer end.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 8425` at `src/cdf.c:1092:5`, and the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of region `[0x625000000100, 0x625000002300)` allocated in `cdf_read_long_sector_chain()`.

parser_admitted.description: By this call the CDF header, SAT, directory, and stream selection have already succeeded, so the PoC has entered SummaryInformation parsing. The saved run immediately logs `cdf.c,594: cdf_calloc 17 512` and then `section len: 8260 properties 18`, proving the witness reaches `cdf_read_property_info()` on the crashing path.

coarse_trace.summary: After CDF container dispatch succeeds, `file_trycdf()` selects the `\005SummaryInformation` user stream and routes it into summary-info parsing.
The parser allocates a 17-sector (`8704`-byte) heap buffer for that stream and copies the attacker-controlled sectors into `scn->sst_tab`.

For property index 5, `cdf_read_property_info()` resolves `q`, computes `left = e - q`, follows the non-vector `CDF_LENGTH32_WSTRING` path, derives `o4` as 4 then 8, parses attacker-controlled length `l`, and accepts the slice because `o4 + l <= left`.
The code stores `s_len/s_buf` for that property but immediately logs the slice with raw `%s`, so `printf` scans beyond `sst_tab` and triggers the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.code:
if ((nr = cdf_read_sector(info, scn->sst_tab, i * ss, ss, h,
    sid)) != CAST(ssize_t, ss)) {
fine_trace.note: Source. After `file_trycdf()` selects `\005SummaryInformation`, this loop copies each attacker-controlled sector into `scn->sst_tab`. The saved run shows the crashing SummaryInformation load allocates `17 * 512 = 8704` bytes at `src/cdf.c:594`, and ASan later identifies this same heap region as the over-read target.

fine_trace.code:
p = CAST(const uint8_t *, cdf_offset(sst->sst_tab, offs + sizeof(sh)));
e = CAST(const uint8_t *, cdf_offset(shp, sh.sh_len));
fine_trace.note: The parser derives the property-table window for this SummaryInformation section inside `sst->sst_tab`. With the saved `offs = 0x30` and `section len: 8260`, `p` points to stream offset `0x38` and `e` to section end `0x2074`; the `p < e` / stream-offset check succeeds, so later property offsets are interpreted within this 8260-byte section.

fine_trace.code:
if ((q = cdf_get_property_info_pos(sst, h, p, e, i)) == NULL)
    goto out;
fine_trace.note: For the crashing iteration `i == 5`, the property-offset table resolves `q` to the fifth property value record at `p + 0xd8`, i.e. stream offset `0x110`. The saved debug line `5) id=0x5 type=0x1f offs=0xd8,0x30` grounds this exact pointer.

This computes the remaining bytes in property 5's record from the section end and the resolved property pointer. With `e = sst_tab + 0x2074` and `q = sst_tab + 0x110`, the saved witness gives `left = 8036`.
This reads property 5's type as `0x1f` (`CDF_LENGTH32_WSTRING`). Because the vector bit is clear, the non-vector string path sets `nelements = 1` and `slen = 1` before the payload offset is derived.
With `slen = 1` on this path, the initial intra-record offset becomes `o4 = 4`. At this point `o4` still points at the stored length field, not the first string byte.

Because the non-vector string path left `slen = 1`, this reads the attacker-controlled 32-bit string length from `q[4]`. The fix later uses this exact `l` as the print bound that the vulnerable `%s` call ignores.
This advances the offset from `4` to `8`, so the later guard and `s_buf` assignment operate on the actual slice start `&q[8]` rather than on the length field.

Present guard. With `o4 = 8` and `left = 8036`, the parsed `l` passes `o4 + l <= left`, so the claimed slice fits inside the 8260-byte section. This check still does not require any NUL terminator inside that slice or before the end of `sst_tab`.

The property is now stored as the accepted slice: `s_len = l` and `s_buf = &q[o4] = &q[8]`. Using the saved offsets (`offs = 0x30`, `q - p = 0xd8`), `s_buf` begins at stream offset `0x118` (`280`) inside the 8704-byte allocation, leaving 8424 addressable bytes before the redzone.

fine_trace.code:
DPRINTF(("o=%" SIZE_T_FORMAT "u l=%d(%"
    SIZE_T_FORMAT "u), t=%" SIZE_T_FORMAT
    "u s=%s\n", o4, l, CDF_ROUND(l, sizeof(l)),
    left, inp[i].pi_str.s_buf));
fine_trace.note: Root cause and sink. In this `CDF_DEBUG` build `DPRINTF` expands to `printf`, and the `%s` conversion consumes `s_buf` as a NUL-terminated C string instead of honoring the already-stored length `l`. The earlier guard from step 9 bounded only the slice within `left`; it did not bound the C-string scan. ASan reports `READ of size 8425` at this call and places the faulting address immediately past `[0x625000000100, 0x625000002300)`, matching a scan from `sst_tab + 0x118` through the 8424 remaining in-bounds bytes to the first redzone byte. The patch fixes this exact call by using `%.*s` and `(int)l`.

allocation_context.note: The over-read pointer aliases the `scn->sst_tab` buffer allocated here. The saved trace reports this object as the 8704-byte region `[0x625000000100, 0x625000002300)`.

It must survive CDF header/directory parsing, expose a `\005SummaryInformation` user stream that `cdf_read_long_sector_chain()` loads as 17 sectors (`8704` bytes), and within that stream make property index 5 parse as `type = 0x1f` at `q - p = 0xd8`. On the non-vector string path the code computes `left = e - q = 8036`, sets `o4 = 4`, reads the 32-bit length at `q[4]`, advances to `o4 = 8`, and the parsed `l` must satisfy `o4 + l <= left`. The bytes starting at `&q[8]` must contain no NUL before the end of `sst_tab`, so the staged `CDF_DEBUG` build's `DPRINTF(..., "%s", s_buf)` scans into the redzone.
